data: Matter is in the realm of our direct experience. Matter exists in different forms. Most common forms are solid, liquid and gas. Other forms of matter could be defined as well. But even among the solids, we encounter variety. Some solids are fragile while others are strong. Many solids expand on heating while some shrink, some liquids flow easily while others are sticky, and so on. Also, matter changes from one state to another on altering external parameters such as the temperature, pressure, electric field, etc. There is an obvious need to go beyond cataloguing these properties. Seeking to understand the basis for this vast variety of properties should be interesting, and could lead to innovations. For instance, the origins for revolution in information technology can be traced back to the availability of semiconductor transistors. This course introduces matter and its forms using the conceptual framework of physics.
